research_question: In children with steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome (including steroid-dependent and frequently relapsing forms), does rituximab compared with tacrolimus (calcineurin inhibitor) reduce the risk of relapse by 12 months?
outcome_description: Occurrence of nephrotic syndrome relapse (proteinuria recurrence per standard ISKDC/KDIGO definitions) within approximately 12 months of randomization; extracted as the number of children experiencing one or more relapses and the total number randomized in each arm.
positive_direction: A positive effect size (RR favoring treatment) means rituximab produced fewer relapses than tacrolimus — i.e. rituximab lowered the risk of relapse by 12 months.
search_queries: rituximab versus tacrolimus steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome children randomized trial
rituximab calcineurin inhibitor relapse-free survival pediatric nephrotic syndrome controlled trial
steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome children relapse rituximab tacrolimus comparison outcome
inclusion_criteria: Study enrolls children or adolescents with steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome (including frequently relapsing or steroid-dependent disease)
Study compares rituximab with tacrolimus (or another calcineurin inhibitor comparator arm) in some form, whether randomized or non-randomized
Study reports any quantitative relapse or remission outcome data (event counts, proportions, rates, or survival/relapse-free estimates) with arm sizes
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, narrative review, editorial, commentary, opinion, case report, or purely theoretical/modeling paper)
No comparison between a rituximab treatment group and a tacrolimus/calcineurin-inhibitor or other control group (single-arm studies only)
No extractable quantitative outcome data to compute an effect size (no relapse event counts or proportions with denominators, and no means+SDs, t/F values, or odds/risk ratios reported)
Completely unrelated to the research topic (e.g. not nephrotic syndrome, not rituximab or tacrolimus, or exclusively adult steroid-resistant populations with no pediatric steroid-sensitive data)
moderators_to_extract: Study design (randomized controlled trial vs non-randomized/observational comparative)
Disease phenotype (frequently relapsing vs steroid-dependent vs mixed)
Rituximab dosing regimen (number/size of infusions, retreatment allowed)
Concomitant/background immunosuppression and steroid tapering protocol
Mean age at enrollment and prior immunosuppressant exposure
Sample size category and country/region of conduct
effect_size_note: Primary pooling as a Risk Ratio using each trial's reported number of children with relapse by ~12 months and the total randomized per arm (intention-to-treat denominators where available). Use a random-effects model (DerSimonian–Laird or REML) with Mantel–Haenszel weighting; apply a continuity correction only when an arm has zero events, and consider Peto OR as a sensitivity check if events are rare. RR < 1 indicates rituximab reduces relapse risk.
